maria: Heads up, after the kernel-selector rollout at 02:10 UTC we saw a ~12% 95th tail latency regression on the MoE inference fleet for batchy chat workloads. Traces point to routing/all-to-all spikes + KV cache churn. :frowning:

perf-bot: (auto) Alert: job=moe-prod, metric=tail_latency_95, change=+12%, window=5m, deploy=kernel-selector-v2 -> investigate.

devin: Can you paste the flame/trace you grabbed?

maria: Pasting the condensed timeline from perf dump (staging repro run):

```
Timeline (ms):
0    - enqueue microbatch
2    - forward start (tp/pipeline)
18   - expert routing (all-to-all)  72ms -> 210ms (after rollout)
282  - kv cache lookup & miss handling  40ms -> 95ms
378  - matmul kernel selection (fused)  40ms
420  - all-reduce(NCCL) waiting  35ms -> 120ms
```

Total step time increased ~220ms compared to baseline. Note the expert routing spike correlates with larger all-to-all payloads (more tokens routed).

ashok: Do we have kernel-selector logs? My guess: selector picked a new packed-gemm kernel that increases launch latency for small-ish tiles; that can hurt the overlap with NCCL. Also scheduler may be serializing communications.

lina: I also saw KV prefetch heuristic disabled for sequences > 512 in the new heuristic PR (it was trying to avoid memory pressure). That explains the KV miss climb. If routing pushes more tokens to same experts, cache pressure + no prefetch -> longer handling.

devin: Oof. So two orthogonal regressions: a kernel change increasing per-chunk CPU/GPU launch latency, and KV prefetch being off causing more cold misses. Both increase time spent before NCCL can overlap.

kevin: Quick check: are we using NCCL async progress? If not, enabling it may allow overlap despite kernel launches. Also check stream ordering: if kernels are being launched on the same stream as collectives, NCCL will block.

maria: deploy-bot shows the rollout window: kernel-selector-v2 rolled to 30% canary at 02:05, to 100% at 02:09. Canary metric looked fine on small sequences. We missed the long-seq MoE traffic in canary.

deploy-bot: rollout: kernel-selector-v2 -> 100% at 02:09 UTC. Canary: 30% -> 100%.

perf-bot: Attached repro script id: repro-1984061723. Summary: routing payload variance up 2.3x, KV miss rate +14%, NCCL wait time +3.2x.

ashok: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) revert kernel-selector-v2 to v1 for the production fleet (quick rollback) 2) re-enable KV prefetch for sequences up to 1024 while we tune memory policy 3) run a microbench for kernel launch overhead and small-tile GEMM.

lina: I can flip the KV prefetch toggle on prod for low-risk stacks in the next 10m. It only affects non-enterprise customers.

devin: I'll prepare a gated rollback for kernel-selector with rollout freeze if we see tail > +8% in next hour. Also want telemetry added to kernel-selector to report chosen kernel id + sequence_len histogram.

kevin: On infra tuning: I'll enable NCCL async progress on a subset of nodes and instrument collectives stream assignment. Also will test launching kernels on a separate compute stream so collectives can progress. Might need to add a cudaEvent barrier to preserve correctness.

maria: For next steps: lina action: toggle KV prefetch; devin: plan rollback if metric exceeds threshold; kevin: try async progress + stream separation in staging; ashok: run microbench to confirm kernel latency regression and suggest kernel thresholds. I'll coordinate and update this thread after we validate.

ashok: One more note: Routing imbalance looks like it amplified because expert assignment now favors fewer experts for specific token patterns (hashing tweak in routing PR). We should test 'entropy' of assignments across typical prompts; if skew increases, that alone could cause hotspotting even without kernel changes.

maria: Good catch. Add to list: revert routing tweak or patch it to more evenly spread until we have a long-tail test.

devin: ack. I'll open a tracking ticket with reproducer and link telemetry dashboards.

kevin: quick perf tip: when reproducing, try scaling the microbatch count per step to expose overlap issues. Small microbatches will surface kernel launch cost; larger will hide it.

maria: Thanks all. Going to schedule a sync after we have staging results. :thumbsup:
